title: Supta Padangushtasana
notes: Supta Padangushtasana is a two-part asana: the first part has twenty vinyasas, the second has twenty-eight.
The 9th and 13th vinyasas are the states of the first part; the 11th and 19th vinyasas are the states of the second part.
Shown here as Part 2, which holds every movement of Part 1; Part 1 alone leaves out the leg to the side (11th–14th on each side).
While in the states of this asana, aspirants must be mindful to practice the breathing methods with attention — Guruji repeats this because the asana is unlike previous ones.

sequence.action: Arms up, palms together, gaze at the fingertips
Fold forward, hands beside the feet, nose to the knees
Lift the head
Jump back: Chaturanga Dandasana
Urdhva Mukha Svanasana
Adho Mukha Svanasana
Lie down on the back, as in the preparations for Sarvangasana, doing rechaka and puraka.

Bring the straightened right leg up toward the head, straighten the left leg, strongly take hold of the big toe of the right leg with the right hand, press the left hand firmly on the left thigh, and lie flat, keeping the head on the floor.
Lift only the head a little, touch the nose to the straightened right knee, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lower the head to the floor.
Bring the right leg out to the right and lower it to the floor, and do rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Raise the right leg, and return to the 8th vinyasa.
Touch the nose to the knee.
Lower the head to the floor.
Lower the right leg to the floor and join the legs together.
Left side: bring the straightened left leg up and take hold of its big toe with the left hand, right hand on the right thigh, head on the floor
Left side: nose to the left knee
Left side: lower the head to the floor
Left side: bring the left leg out to the left and lower it to the floor; rechaka and puraka as much as possible
Left side: raise the left leg, holding the big toe
Left side: nose to the knee
Left side: lower the head to the floor
Left side: lower the left leg to the floor and join the legs

Come into the position of Halasana, press the hands to the floor by the ears, and roll the whole body back over the head into the position of the 4th vinyasa (Chaturanga Dandasana). This is called Chakrasana.
Urdhva Mukha Svanasana
Adho Mukha Svanasana
Jump the feet between the hands, lift the head
Fold, nose to the knees
Urdhva Hastasana: arms up, hands together, look at the fingertips
Samasthiti

benefits: Supta Padangushtasana purifies and strengthens the waist region, knees, food and anal channels, and the sperm passageway (virya nala).
It dissolves the bad fat on the sides of the body and the waist, making the waist slender and strong, and the body light.
quotes: Indeed, whatever the asana, one should practice first on the right side and then on the left side.
